name: Law of Similarity
description: Elements that look alike in color, shape, size, type style, or another visual property are perceived as belonging together. Visual sameness acts like an implicit label.
design_relevance_note: Supports consistent component styling, chart legends, status-chip systems, list scanning, and grouping related controls without extra separators.
prevalence_note: A core Gestalt grouping law used constantly in visual hierarchy, component systems, chart design, and information grouping; standard UX/UI teaching material.

findings.description: Reviewing a century of Gestalt and modern vision-science work, Wagemans et al. conclude that classical grouping principles such as proximity and similarity — along with newer principles such as uniform connectedness — remain core, empirically studied mechanisms of perceptual organization, with documented roles in contour integration and figure-ground organization.
findings.source_title: A century of Gestalt psychology in visual perception: I. Perceptual grouping and figure-ground organization.

findings.description: Using EEG time-frequency analysis, Ma et al. found that grouping interface color swatches by the Gestalt similarity principle (shared hue, varying saturation/brightness) reduced activation in delta/theta/gamma EEG bands over parietal and occipital regions and lowered self-reported emotional arousal, while increasing self-reported visual comfort, compared to equivalent color quantity presented without similarity-based grouping — physiological evidence that Gestalt similarity grouping mitigates the perceptual-overload cost of high color quantity in an interface.
findings.source_title: Applying gestalt similarity to improve visual perception of interface color quantity: An EEG study

applications.title: Etsy distinguishes 'Free Shipping' and 'Bestseller' badges by pairing color with an icon
applications.description: Nielsen Norman Group's article on the similarity principle describes how Etsy's homepage marks some products with 'Free Shipping' and 'Bestseller' indicator badges. Rather than styling both badges identically, Etsy gives them different background colors and adds a distinguishing icon to the Bestseller badge -- deliberately keeping the two indicators visually dissimilar enough that users can tell them apart quickly, avoiding the confusion that would result if same-shaped badges only in different colors, or worse, in the same color, were used side by side.
applications.ethical_note: A clarity technique that helps users scan and distinguish product badges faster, with no persuasive or manipulative dimension.

applications.title: Synchrony Bank's same-color buttons blended a primary action in with secondary ones
applications.description: Nielsen Norman Group's article on the similarity principle describes how the Submit button in Synchrony Bank's Message Center shared the same green color as the Cancel and Add Attachment buttons, causing all three to be perceived as belonging to the same group of equally-weighted actions. Because same-color elements are read as sharing the same function and importance, users had to spend extra time figuring out which button was actually the primary, form-submitting action rather than a secondary one.
applications.ethical_note: A visual-hierarchy usability shortcoming (users must work harder to find the primary action), with no persuasive or manipulative dimension either way.
